claims.claim: This is a scrap LG Flatron TV that is currently not functioning properly.
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a small CRT television with a dark screen; no powered-on picture quality or clear brand/model label is visible.

claims.claim: It is being sold as is for parts or recycling.
claims.evidence: The report does not show internal parts, dismantling, or any explicit 'for parts' marking; only the TV exterior is visible.
Pickup responsibility is not shown in the photos.

risks.risk: Brand/model may not be LG Flatron (CRT sets often have different labels; witness could not read any brand/model).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the brand/model label on the back or side (nameplate/sticker) and any model number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as generic non-working CRT TV for parts/recycling (worst case).

risks.risk: Condition may be worse than 'not functioning' (e.g., dead power supply, short, or damaged CRT), which affects scrap value and safe handling.
risks.proof: A short clip of the TV being powered on showing whether it lights up (standby/neck glow), and whether it stays on or shuts down/flickers.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as non-working/for parts with no guarantee of repairability.

risks.risk: Screen may be partially functional (e.g., shows lines/low brightness) which could raise value if it can display an image.
risks.proof: A powered-on test shot showing a clear picture (any channel/input) with color/lines/brightness visible.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst case: no usable picture.

risks.risk: Missing/unknown accessories and controls (remote, cables) reduce usability and resale value.
risks.proof: Photos of included items: remote control (if any), power cable, and any AV/antenna cables; plus a photo of the control panel working.

risks.risk: Physical damage to cabinet/stand (cracks, dents, rust) can reduce scrap value and increase transport risk.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the cabinet corners, screen bezel edges, and the base/stand attachment points.
risks.if_unproven: Priced assuming possible wear/damage typical for used CRT.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the back/side label showing brand and exact model number.
Short video clip of the TV powered on (show standby light/neck glow and whether it stays on).
Powered-on test showing any picture (even if poor): lines, brightness, color balance.
Photos of all ports (AV/antenna/SCART/HDMI if present) and a quick check that inputs are accessible.
Photo of the control buttons area and whether volume/channel controls respond.
Photos of the cabinet and stand/base for cracks/dents/rust; include close-ups of corners and mounting points.
Photo of included accessories (remote, power cable, any AV/antenna cables) or confirmation that none are included.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a small CRT TV with a dark screen and no evidence of working condition; brand/model and functionality are not verifiable from the provided images, so it should be priced at the worst case as non-working CRT for parts/recycling.
